items.q: Which glycosaminoglycan is unique because it is entirely non-sulfated, is not covalently attached to a core protein, and is synthesized at the plasma membrane rather than in the Golgi apparatus?
items.exp: Hyaluronic acid is an enormous non-sulfated GAG composed of D-glucuronic acid and N-acetylglucosamine. It is synthesized by plasma membrane hyaluronan synthases and acts as a central backbone for proteoglycan aggregates.
r: Correct. Hyaluronic acid is non-sulfated, lacks covalent protein core attachment, and is made at the plasma membrane.
Incorrect. Chondroitin sulfate is sulfated and linked to core proteins in Golgi.
Incorrect. Heparan sulfate is sulfated in Golgi.
Incorrect. Keratan sulfate is sulfated.
items.kp: Hyaluronic acid is the only non-sulfated GAG not covalently bound to a core protein; it is synthesized at the cell surface to serve as the backbone for proteoglycan aggregates.

items.q: In articular cartilage, how do chondroitin sulfate and keratan sulfate chains attached to aggrecan confer resistance to compressive biomechanical forces?
o: Abundant negative sulfate and carboxyl charges repel each other and attract hydrated sodium cations, creating a swollen elastic cushion
They form rigid triple helices that resist bending
They form covalent crosslinks with mineralized hydroxyapatite
They polymerize into insoluble cross-beta sheet fibrils
items.exp: Dense negative charges on sulfate and carboxyl groups create charge repulsion, keeping GAG chains extended. They attract Na+ ions and water, creating osmotic swelling pressure that resists compressive joint loading.
r: Correct. Negative charge density attracts water to generate osmotic swelling pressure against compression.
Incorrect. Triple helices are characteristic of collagen.
Incorrect. Proteoglycans do not crosslink mineral directly in cartilage.
Incorrect. Beta-sheet fibrils describe amyloid.
items.kp: The high negative charge density of sulfated GAGs attracts water and sodium, generating high swelling pressure that absorbs compressive mechanical loads in articular cartilage.

items.q: A 2-year-old child presents with coarse facial features, corneal clouding, hepatosplenomegaly, umbilical hernia, and severe dysostosis multiplex on skeletal survey. What is the diagnosis and deficient enzyme?
o: Hunter syndrome (MPS II), iduronate sulfatase deficiency
Sanfilippo syndrome (MPS III), heparan sulfamidase deficiency
items.exp: Hurler syndrome (MPS I) is an autosomal recessive deficiency of alpha-L-iduronidase. Dermatan and heparan sulfate accumulate, causing coarse facial features, severe corneal clouding, dysostosis multiplex, and mental deficiency.
r: Correct. Hurler syndrome features alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency with corneal clouding and dysostosis.
Incorrect. Hunter syndrome is X-linked and lacks corneal clouding.
Incorrect. Sanfilippo syndrome presents with childhood dementia and mild skeletal changes.
Incorrect. Morquio syndrome features skeletal dysplasia with normal intellect and clear corneas.
items.kp: Hurler syndrome (MPS I) is caused by autosomal recessive alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency, marked by coarse facies, corneal clouding, dysostosis multiplex, and intellectual disability.

Autosomal recessive inheritance and severe corneal clouding
Accumulation of keratan sulfate without heparan sulfate
items.exp: Hunter syndrome is caused by iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency. It is unique among the mucopolysaccharidoses in being X-linked recessive, and affected boys characteristically have clear corneas (no corneal clouding).

Incorrect. Hurler syndrome is autosomal recessive with corneal clouding.
Incorrect. Cardiomyopathy occurs in Pompe disease and late MPS.
Incorrect. Dermatan and heparan sulfate accumulate in both MPS I and II.

items.q: A 4-year-old boy presents with progressive behavioral hyperactivity, sleep disturbances, loss of speech milestones, and aggressive outbursts, but minimal skeletal deformities and no corneal clouding. What is the diagnosis?
o: Sanfilippo syndrome (MPS III), impaired heparan sulfate degradation
items.exp: Sanfilippo syndrome (MPS III) involves failure to degrade heparan sulfate exclusively. It presents primarily with severe, progressive central nervous system neurodegeneration, sleep disruption, and hyperactivity with mild somatic features.
r: Correct. Sanfilippo syndrome is marked by severe progressive dementia and hyperactivity from heparan sulfate accumulation.
Incorrect. Hurler syndrome has prominent somatic and corneal features.
Incorrect. Gaucher disease causes splenomegaly and bone crises.
Incorrect. Tay-Sachs causes infantile regression with cherry-red spot.

items.q: Morquio syndrome (MPS IV) is distinct from other mucopolysaccharidoses because patients have severe skeletal dysplasia (short trunk dwarfism, pectus carinatum, odontoid hypoplasia) but retain which physiological attribute?
o: Completely normal intelligence and intellectual development
items.exp: Morquio syndrome (defective keratan sulfate breakdown) causes severe skeletal dysplasia and atlantoaxial instability from odontoid hypoplasia, but intelligence is completely normal because keratan sulfate is absent from brain parenchyma.
r: Correct. Morquio syndrome patients have preserved normal intellect despite severe skeletal dysplasia.
Incorrect. Skeletal dysplasia is severe.
Incorrect. Heart valves frequently develop regurgitation.
Incorrect. Urine is positive for keratan sulfate.

items.q: What is the specific trisaccharide linker that covalently attaches glycosaminoglycan chains to serine residues of core proteins in proteoglycans?
items.exp: Proteoglycan O-linked synthesis begins in the ER/Golgi with the attachment of xylose to a core protein serine, followed by two galactose residues, forming the universal Xylose-Gal-Gal linker.
r: Correct. Xylose-Gal-Gal is the universal linker trisaccharide.
Incorrect. Glucose-glucose-mannose is not the linker.
Incorrect. Mannose-GlcNAc is found in N-linked glycoprotein cores.
Incorrect. Sialic acid is a terminal capping sugar.

items.exp: Heparin contains a unique pentasaccharide sequence that binds antithrombin III, inducing a conformational change that accelerates AT-III inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa by up to 1,000-fold.

Incorrect. Protein C is activated by thrombomodulin.
Incorrect. TFPI inhibits Xa/tissue factor.
Incorrect. Alpha-2 antiplasmin inhibits plasmin.

items.q: I-cell disease (mucolipidosis II) is a severe lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficiency of GlcNAc phosphotransferase. Why do lysosomal acid hydrolases fail to reach lysosomes?
o: Failure to phosphorylate mannose residues to mannose-6-phosphate in the Golgi routes enzymes to the extracellular default secretion pathway
Enzymes are degraded in the proteasome by ERAD
Lysosomal membranes lack vacuolar proton pumps
Enzymes undergo premature peptide cleavage in rough ER
items.exp: Mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) is the recognition tag that targets acid hydrolases from the Golgi to lysosomes. Without GlcNAc phosphotransferase, enzymes lack M6P and are default-secreted into plasma, causing empty lysosomes with inclusion bodies.
r: Correct. Absent M6P tag causes mistargeting of lysosomal hydrolases into extracellular blood.
Incorrect. Enzymes fold normally and escape ERAD.
Incorrect. Proton pumps are intact.
Incorrect. Synthesis in ER is normal.
items.kp: I-cell disease results from GlcNAc phosphotransferase deficiency; lacking the mannose-6-phosphate sorting tag, lysosomal enzymes are secreted into plasma, leaving empty inclusion-filled lysosomes.

Incorrect. Enzyme replacement is not established for Sanfilippo.
